name: pen_merge
description: Polygon pen merge: links decided at the gesture (cells: scene merge radius and latching; cells_k_b3: radii after an edge snap; edge_press: stroke-edge and scene-edge presses).

provenance.notes: fresh GUI worker per cell, NEW empty foreground mesh; scene vertex V script-placed at a measured click landing + an offset; clicks/drags/typing are real input; one readback after the last gesture.

rig.view: top orthographic unless a cell says otherwise; default zoom 440 px per metre (merge distance 3 px of world = 0.0068255 m); wheel zoom x2^(1/4) per step
rig.click_quantum: a clicked position is rounded to a zoom-dependent quantum: 0.005 m at 440 px/m, 0.002 at 622, 0.01 at 110 (the earlier placement fixture's 0.01 at 440 is a coincidence of its pixels)
rig.scene_geometry: pre-existing vertices/triangles are created in the SAME foreground mesh before the tool activates (they stand for committed geometry); new points come only from real pointer clicks/drags and panel typing

law: Merge is decided by the POINTER GESTURE, never by a later weld: (1) a click or drag-end whose pointer lies within R screen pixels (24 < R < 28, the same at 110 and 440 px/m, blind to depth) of a vertex of the edited mesh makes the stroke point TAKE that vertex's 3-D position and SHARE its index (the decision is latched at the gesture: zooming before the commit changes nothing); (2) a clicked point whose mirror (symmetry on) is closer than the merge distance (gap 2|x| < 3 px of view-wide world size; same value in perspective at any depth) shares one vertex with its mirror, the original's position survives; (3) a click on an existing point of the live stroke selects it and adds nothing; (4) typed positions never merge (not with scene vertices, not with mirrors, even when exactly coincident). merge off disables (1) and (2).

law_k_c2: Merge vs global snapping (snapping ON, vertex type off): (1) grid snapping quantises the pointer first (grid distance 100% = always); the merge then searches a vertex within the ordinary merge radius (~24 px) of the QUANTISED point (the raw pointer's distance does not decide); (2) an element snap (edge) in range places the point and beats a NEARER merge vertex; after it, only a vertex within ~4.4-5 px of the SNAPPED point links (linked at 4.4 px, not at 5.0/5.5/6.0 px; never at 19.5 px); (3) no endpoint capture by edge snapping; (4) snapping on with no type enabled leaves the merge unchanged. Linked points: a drag end re-decides the link from the drag-end pointer (40 px away -> unlinked new vertex, V unmoved; 10 px -> re-linked); a typed edit unlinks (new vertex at the typed position, V unmoved).
law_k_b3: after an EDGE snap places the point E (merge on), the merge links: a vertex of the snapped edge itself within ~15.4-19.5 SCREEN px of E (linked at 2.2/4.4/11/15.4 px at 440, 4.4 and 12.1 px at 110 (0.04/0.11 m), 7.04 px at 880; not 19.5 px at 440 (K-C2), not 29.9 px at 880 (0.034 m)); any OTHER vertex only within ~2.2-3.5 screen px (linked 2.2 px perpendicular and 2.2 px along the edge at 440; not 3.5 px perpendicular at 110/440/880 = 0.032/0.008/0.004 m) -- both radii are screen-space (a world radius is refuted by both families). Vertex snap + merge: the snapped point links V (shares its index)
